messages.content: What are the different properties of Hydrogen?

message.content:
**Hydrogen (H)** – the simplest and most abundant element in the universe – has a range of distinctive physical, chemical, and nuclear properties:

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Symbol** | H |
| **Standard atomic weight** | ~1.008 u (average of isotopes) |
| **Isotopes** | ¹H (protium, 99.98 %), ²H (deuterium, 0.02 %) and trace amounts of ³H (tritium). |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Electron affinity** | –72.8 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| **Boiling point** | –252.9 °C (20.44 K) at 1 atm |
| **Melting point** | –259.2 °C (14.05 K) at 1 atm |
| **Density at STP** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (≈0.00008988 kg m⁻³) |
| **Molar volume at STP** | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| **Reactivity** | Highly reactive; forms hydrides with metals, reacts with halogens, acids, and oxidants. |
| **Bonding** | Forms covalent bonds (H₂), ionic bonds (as H⁺ or H⁻), and participates in hydrogen bonding (in water, alcohols, etc.). |
| **Acidity/Basicity** | Acts as a weak acid (forming H₃O⁺ in aqueous solution) and a weak base (forming OH⁻ when deprotonated). |
| **Oxidation states** | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride ions), 0 (molecular H₂). |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible), Paschen series (IR). |
| **Nuclear spin** | Protium (I=½), Deuterium (I=1), Tritium (I=½). |
| **Applications** | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells), rocket propellant, industrial hydrogenation, laboratory standard gas, medical imaging (MRI contrast agents with deuterium). |

These values illustrate why hydrogen is central to chemistry, physics, and many technologies—from stellar fusion to clean‑energy vehicles.
